observation: A prior camera-relative drag comparison passed even though the rig transformed the physical orbit axis into a tilted axis; the owner still experienced unwanted tumbling after quick top views.
cause: The test oracle cancelled the pose transform in camera-local coordinates and therefore could not establish model-relative yaw or uprightness.
proposed_rule: Matching camera-relative motion does not prove consistent model-relative orbit. Verify the physical axis, constant inclination under yaw and pole behavior against an independent unmodified default controller. For the owner's Z-up turntable, horizontal drags always yaw around model Z; exact top/bottom yaw spins within the plane, and inward pitch leaves the pole without a roll jump. Quick presets change pose, not the model coordinate frame, geometry or selection/display state. Mark a pose inactive after manual orbit leaves it.
limits: Supersedes the camera-local equivalence claim in pose-only-quick-views-preserve-default-orbit; retain that and earlier records as history. Z-up turntable is this owner's selected interaction convention, not a universal requirement for all 3D applications. Phone checks are viewport emulation, not hardware acceptance. No fabrication or source-geometry approval.
